page: Microsoft Azure D8pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft's ARM architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running on ARM Neoverse-N2 processors clocked at 3.4 GHz, avoiding hyperthreading concurrency issues. Memory capacity is set to 32.0 GB (4.0 GB per core) backed by 128 MB of L3 cache. For local storage, the instance includes an integrated 472 GB NVMe SSD, while GPU hardware is not included.

Benchmark results show balanced general-purpose execution across multi-core and memory subsystems. PassMark memory testing ranks in the top 10% with a score of 3089.48, supported by large-block read bandwidth of 155.37 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression reaching a strong 33.04 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks fall squarely within the middle 50%, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 9383.0 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 16570.31.

The hardware configuration entails notable performance tradeoffs. While database and in-memory caches show consistent throughput (15.9 million Redis SET operations per second and 9902.31 PassMark database operations), specialized workloads encounter bottlenecks. Cryptographic operations show weakness, with PassMark encryption scoring 1493.18 (bottom 25%). Similarly, LLM inference performance drops considerably on medium 7B parameter models, registering 12.33 tokens/sec for prompt processing (bottom 10%).

Given its dedicated ARM core topology, balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, and bundled high-speed NVMe storage, the D8pds_v6 delivers solid cost efficiency for general compute. It is suitable for web serving, microservices, software compilation, CI/CD pipelines, caching layers, and relational or operational databases requiring fast local scratch disks.
